state.invariant: Pending or accepted resolution seals admission; a resolution is accepted once per generation over exactly the admitted responses (at least one), resolves only via the exact pending operation, and reopen of a resolved request advances the generation.

code_behavior.write_while_pending: Comment/revise on a request with a pending resolution at the current revision is refused with Conflict marked transient (retry when it settles); no fact appended.
code_behavior.write_while_resolved: Comment/revise on a resolved request at the current revision is refused with Conflict, non-transient (reopen first); no fact appended.
code_behavior.second_resolve_while_pending: A second Resolve command with a new command id while one is pending is refused with transient Conflict, revision unchanged.
code_behavior.reopen: Reopen of a resolved request advances generation 1 to 2 and revision by 1; a comment then admitted carries generation 2.
code_behavior.whole_history_set: Resolution must name every response admitted across all generations, not only the current generation.

state.tests: Three tests assert: pending => comment, revise and second resolve all Conflict transient with unchanged revision; resolved => comment and revise Conflict non-transient with unchanged revision; reopen => generation 2, revision+1, admitted comment has generation 2.

pending_seal.instructions: Is the pending-state behavior in state.code_behavior consistent with state.invariant?

criteria.consistent: Refusing all writes and a second resolution while pending, without appending a fact, enforces the seal.
criteria.inconsistent: The behavior does not enforce the seal.

transient_vs_state.instructions: Is it right that pending is a transient conflict while resolved is a non-transient state conflict?

criteria.right: Pending settles by itself, so retry is valid; resolved needs reopen.
criteria.wrong: Both should have the same transience.

whole_history.instructions: For state.code_behavior.whole_history_set, is requiring all-generation responses consistent with state.invariant 'exactly the admitted responses'?

criteria.whole_history: Consistent: admitted responses means all admitted on the stream.

tests_assert_invariant.instructions: The three tests in state.tests assert the invariant in state.invariant behaviorally (facts not appended, generation advanced).
